projects.title: Insight / Papertrail
projects.description:
Deployed an automated program management review process which unified legacy SRA and CSGov reporting systems though a common program performance language, set of measures, and process; significantly decreased report workload; and increased the number of programs monitored from ~240 to over 640. This included participation in over 100 in depth Group PMRs monthly by CSRA program management senior experts. Part of the results was a comprehensive database on program performance which allows CSRA to analyse program performance across nine dimensions of performance and determine corporate trends. This had a direct impact on improving program performance across the company as the number of green programs increased from 49% to 67%. Reductions in percentages of Red and Yellow programs also improved profitability across the company.

Utilized Apache Storm + Spring Data JPA for ingesting data into the database (PostgreSQL), NodeJS for back-end logic, and AngularJS to create dynamic web pages. In addition to software development, I was very involved with the design of the application; frequently meeting with the UX designer and product owner outside of scheduled meetings. For the majority of these projects I was one of the lead developers. Following the initial release, I became the technical lead.

Screenshots and videos available upon request.

projects.title: Stormfall
projects.description:
This was a semester long project I had for my first software engineering course. I worked in a team with five other people, students from the art department, and our client, DelDOT (Delaware Department of Transportation), to produce a game to educate children in the importance of storm drain management. Our duties included constructing storyboards, presenting to our client, and coding the game from scratch. 

Please keep in mind that we had many limitations, such as constraints set by our client (ex. could not use keyboard, only mouse), and the fact that we had such a short time to complete the project.
